alignments.note: No English determiner is written for 'of ignorance', so the article anchors nothing (rules 21, 23).
Genitive noun with its case preposition (rule 21).
The ASV writes no word for the correlative μέν; marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it (rule 70).
Article before the divine name with no English determiner (rule 23).

Circumstantial participle converted into a coordinate finite clause, rendered by the finite 'overlooked'; rule 88 puts the juncture the conversion requires on the finite verb it introduces and never on the participle it follows.
The nominalizing article of the adverbial τὰ νῦν contributes no part of the English 'now', which answers wholly to the adverb (rules 23, 61, 93).

Main finite verb with its English subject; the supplied juncture 'but' is a rule 7 helper on the finite verb it introduces, exactly as rule 88's ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν → 'cast them down to hell, and committed them' puts the juncture on the main verb after a participle converted into a finite clause. Discontinuous around 'now' under rule 15. Marking 'but' added under rule 86 remains defensible, but rule 88 refuses that where a participle stands in the clause to license the juncture.
No English determiner is written for 'men', so the article anchors nothing (rules 21, 23).
Infinitive expanded into a finite clause; the supplied complementizer, subject and modal are its helpers (rules 7, 85), discontinuous under rule 15.

review_notes: Corrected the placement of 'but'. The accepted alignment gave it to the article of the adverbial τὰ νῦν, but an article contributes no part of such a fused adverbial expression (rule 93's principle), and 'now' answers wholly to νῦν. The verse is rule 88's shape — a circumstantial participle (ὑπεριδών) converted into a coordinate finite clause with the juncture standing before the main finite verb — so 'but' is a helper on παραγγέλλει, as rule 88's own ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν precedent has it.

Marking 'but' added under rule 86 was considered and rejected: rule 86's test is whether a source token licenses the word, and rule 88 names a participle standing in the same clause as exactly such a token. The competing reading is recorded in the verb's note.
μέν remains unrepresented under rule 70; the correlation it marks is not a word the ASV wrote for the particle.
